interfaces.name: Box web application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, menus and forms of a persistent, navigable representation of Box content.

provenance.evidence: References the Box Web App as the surface where users work with content.

interfaces.name: Box mobile app
interfaces.classification_rationale: A first-party mobile client whose actions are affordance manipulation on a mobile UI; counted separately from the web client per the surface checklist.

provenance.evidence: Box lists first-party desktop and mobile app downloads.
Box's own App Store listing for the mobile client.

interfaces.name: Box Drive desktop client
interfaces.technology: Windows/macOS desktop app mounting Box in Finder/Explorer
interfaces.classification_rationale: Content is presented as a navigable file-system volume whose items the user manipulates as affordances of the OS explorer.

provenance.evidence: Box Drive streams Box content into Finder/File Explorer for direct manipulation.
Official Box Drive desktop downloads for Mac and Windows.

interfaces.name: Box REST API
interfaces.technology: REST over HTTPS, base api.box.com/2.0, OAuth 2.0
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations via structured HTTPS requests; Box AI and Sign APIs share the same base, auth and invocation style and fold in here.

provenance.evidence: API reference covering every Box resource under api.box.com/2.0 with OAuth 2.0.

interfaces.name: Box CLI command interface
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed as explicit commands (e.g. box folders:get 0); no persistent navigable TUI is exposed, so it is a single command interface.

provenance.evidence: Box CLI for managing Box content from the terminal via commands.

interfaces.name: Box FTPS service
interfaces.technology: FTPS/FTPES service at ftp.box.com over TLS
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer invokes file-transfer operations through the FTP command set over TLS; distinct base and auth from the REST API.

provenance.evidence: Box supports FTPS/FTPES for bulk upload/download via ftp.box.com.

interfaces.name: Box SFTP service
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer invokes file operations over the SSH File Transfer Protocol; protocol, endpoint and auth differ from FTPS and from REST, so it is a separate interface.

provenance.evidence: RFC-compliant SFTP service via sftp.services.box.com:22; GA Sept 2025 (current), superseding older 'not supported' posts.

interfaces.name: Box Webhooks (V1/V2)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Box initiates the interaction on file/folder events and delivers the payload to a consumer-controlled receiver URL.

provenance.evidence: Webhooks monitor Box content for events and notify a URL of the consumer's choice.

interfaces.name: Box AI in-product assistant
interfaces.technology: Natural-language chat panel in web/mobile (Box AI, Box Agent, AI Home)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer interacts through natural-language messages interpreted by the service, with tool orchestration internal and not exposed as a discovery contract.

provenance.evidence: Message box, Ask, follow-up questions and conversation history in the Box AI panel.

interfaces.name: Box remote MCP server
interfaces.classification_rationale: The interaction contract exposes semantically described tools that agent consumers discover and select; discovery/selection structure the contract, so Agentic rather than Programmatic.

provenance.evidence: Box-hosted remote MCP server at mcp.box.com exposing content and AI tools to agents (GA Aug 2025).

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Same base/auth/invocation as REST API; part of it, not a separate interface
No persistent navigable TUI; CLI is command-only
Open-source community project self-hosted by the consumer; not a provider-operated endpoint; same paradigm as the remote server
Front-end component library for building UIs, not a provider interface
A way to call the REST API, not a separate interface

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Box Notes / Sign / Hubs / Doc Gen / AI Studio
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Features/products within the web app or REST API, not distinct access mechanisms

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Third-party integrations (Salesforce, Teams, Slack, Office add-ins, Snowflake, Airbyte)
